indirect_variant.behaviour: Ask what slows the work down or gets lost on the way up, and write every answer down.
indirect_variant.observable: you hold a written note about the process that you recognise as being about you

moves.trigger: the opening of the next skip-level
moves.behaviour: Tell the room what you changed because of the last note, and what you could not change.
moves.first_failure: you will describe a change nobody below you could see.
moves.observable: somebody below you names the change without being told
moves.retire_when: people cite a change you made when they raise the next thing
moves.author: claude-draft

indirect_variant.behaviour: Tell the middle manager what you changed and why, so their team hears it through them.
indirect_variant.observable: the team knows what changed and where it came from, and heard it from their own manager

moves.trigger: your one-to-ones with direct reports, monthly
moves.behaviour: Ask each direct report to run one skip-level of their own and bring back one uncomfortable note.
moves.first_failure: they will bring back good news, and you will accept it.
moves.observable: a direct report hands you a note about their own area that they did not enjoy receiving
moves.retire_when: the notes arrive without you asking for them
moves.author: claude-draft

moves.trigger: the standing operational meeting, weekly
moves.behaviour: State the problem as one fact with a number attached, and stop talking.
moves.first_failure: you will attach blame to the fact and the room will defend your predecessor.
moves.observable: the number gets repeated by somebody else within a fortnight
moves.retire_when: the problem is on somebody else's agenda without you putting it there
moves.author: jim

indirect_variant.behaviour: Put the number on the shared review and ask the room what it tells them. Then say yours.
indirect_variant.observable: somebody in the room names the problem from the number, and your reading is on the record beside theirs

moves.trigger: the weekly operational meeting, once somebody else is repeating the number
moves.behaviour: Ask who owns the number and when it will next be reported. Write both in the minutes.
moves.first_failure: you will volunteer to own it yourself, and it becomes your problem again.
moves.observable: the minutes carry a name and a date against the number
moves.retire_when: the number is reported on its date without anyone chasing it
moves.author: claude-draft

indirect_variant.behaviour: Before the meeting, ask the sponsor whose agenda the number belongs on, and let them assign it.
indirect_variant.observable: the sponsor names an owner in the meeting and the minutes carry the name and a date

moves.trigger: a monthly skip-level with the people nearest the work
moves.behaviour: Ask which number they watch that nobody above them looks at. Put one on the review.
moves.first_failure: they will tell you nothing is wrong, because saying so has cost people here before. Ask for the number and leave the opinion out.
moves.observable: a number from below your level appears on the review with its finder's name against it
moves.retire_when: problems reach the review before they reach you
moves.author: claude-draft

moves.trigger: a one-to-one with each former peer, once, in the first month. Hardest first
moves.behaviour: Name what changes, what does not, and what you will now decide alone.
moves.first_failure: you will soften it into a chat and leave without having said the middle part.
moves.observable: the other person can repeat back what you now decide alone
moves.retire_when: every peer has had the conversation
moves.author: jim

indirect_variant.behaviour: Put the new sign-off route in writing, then take each former peer through it over their own work.
indirect_variant.observable: each former peer has heard the new route from you before it touched a decision of theirs

moves.trigger: the team meeting where the first decision you took alone gets announced
moves.behaviour: Announce the decision, say you took it alone, and take the questions yourself.
moves.first_failure: you will say 'we decided'. Say 'I decided'.
moves.observable: the room hears 'I decided' and the decision still stands a week later
moves.retire_when: former peers bring decisions to you without being told to
moves.author: claude-draft

indirect_variant.behaviour: Circulate the decision in writing under your name before the meeting, then take questions on the work.
indirect_variant.observable: the written decision carries your name alone and the meeting discusses how to deliver it

moves.trigger: the weekly allocation of work, where old friends expect a favour
moves.behaviour: Allocate on the merits, and say the reason for each allocation out loud in the room.
moves.first_failure: you will skip the reason when the work goes to an old friend. That is the one to say.
moves.observable: each allocation this week has a reason the room heard
moves.retire_when: nobody reads an allocation as a favour or a snub
moves.author: claude-draft

moves.trigger: the next thing you publish or send widely
moves.behaviour: Write what you intend to do in the role before you write what the role is.
moves.first_failure: you will look at what other people wrote first. Do not.
moves.observable: the first line contains an intention, not a title
moves.retire_when: you stop looking at what other people wrote
moves.author: jim

indirect_variant.behaviour: Write your intent as your part in a problem the organisation already names, and show your sponsor first.
indirect_variant.observable: the sponsor has read it before it goes out, and its first line names a shared problem and your part in it

moves.trigger: the next meeting where you are introduced to a new group
moves.behaviour: Say your intention out loud in the same words you wrote, before anyone asks what you do.
moves.first_failure: you will paraphrase it into something safer on the way out.
moves.observable: the words you said match the words you wrote
moves.retire_when: people quote your intention back in your own words
moves.author: claude-draft

indirect_variant.behaviour: Circulate your written intention before the meeting, then open by pointing to it.
indirect_variant.observable: people arrive having read it and ask about it

moves.trigger: your own calendar, the first working day of each quarter
moves.behaviour: Reread your stated intention, mark what happened against it, and send the update to the same list.
moves.first_failure: you will rewrite the intention to fit what happened.
moves.observable: the update went out with the original intention unchanged at the top
moves.retire_when: people ask for the update before the quarter ends
moves.author: claude-draft

moves.trigger: every conversation with somebody who could buy
moves.behaviour: End with a specific next thing and a date, out loud.
moves.first_failure: you will end on 'let me know', which is not a next thing.
moves.observable: a date exists in somebody else's calendar
moves.retire_when: you notice yourself doing it without deciding to
moves.author: jim

indirect_variant.behaviour: Offer a working session on the buyer's problem, with a date, and say it could lead to work.
indirect_variant.observable: a working session sits in the buyer's calendar, and the buyer knows it is a step towards work

moves.trigger: the second meeting with a buyer who has shown interest
moves.behaviour: Name the fee range out loud before the buyer asks for it.
moves.first_failure: you will name a range so wide it commits nobody. Name the number you would accept.
moves.observable: the buyer has answered a number you said
moves.retire_when: saying the fee costs you nothing in the room
moves.author: claude-draft

indirect_variant.behaviour: Send a written scope with the fee on it before the meeting, and walk through it together.
indirect_variant.observable: the buyer raises the fee first, from the page you sent

moves.trigger: Monday morning, alone, with the list of open buyers
moves.behaviour: List every open buyer with the next dated step. Any line without a date gets a call today.
moves.first_failure: the list will be longer than you thought, and you will call the easiest one first.
moves.observable: every line on the list carries a date
moves.retire_when: no line on Monday's list is missing a date
moves.author: claude-draft

moves.trigger: your own calendar, Friday
moves.behaviour: Mark last week as old job or new job, and name a successor for one block.
moves.first_failure: you will name a successor and keep doing it anyway.
moves.observable: a block on next week's calendar has somebody else's name on it
moves.retire_when: the old-job blocks are gone
moves.author: jim

indirect_variant.behaviour: Bring the successor into the client's next meetings, then step back once the client calls them.
indirect_variant.observable: the client has been told who does the work, and calls the successor first

moves.trigger: the next time a client calls or writes to you about work you have handed on
moves.behaviour: Name the successor, copy them in, and let them send the answer.
moves.first_failure: you will answer the question first and introduce the successor afterwards.
moves.observable: the successor sent the answer and the client replied to them
moves.retire_when: clients go to the successor without routing through you
moves.author: claude-draft

indirect_variant.behaviour: Reply with the successor in copy, answer in one line, and let them carry the rest.
indirect_variant.observable: the thread continues between the client and the successor

moves.trigger: your one-to-one with the successor, a month after the handover
moves.behaviour: Ask your successor what they still do from their old job, and name a block they hand down.
moves.first_failure: they will say nothing, because you are the reason they still do it.
moves.observable: the successor's calendar has a block with somebody else's name on it
moves.retire_when: the successor runs the Friday marking without you
moves.author: claude-draft

moves.trigger: the weekly meeting where you usually stay quiet
moves.behaviour: Say one sentence in the first ten minutes. Any sentence. Then go back to listening.
moves.first_failure: you will wait for the perfect moment and the meeting will end.
moves.observable: you spoke, and it was early
moves.retire_when: speaking early stops costing you anything
moves.author: jim

indirect_variant.behaviour: Before the meeting, give the chair your one sentence and ask them to call on you early.
indirect_variant.observable: the chair brings you in during the first ten minutes and you say the sentence yourself

moves.trigger: the weekly meeting, when a decision is about to close
moves.behaviour: Before the decision closes, say the one thing you would change, and the reason, in two sentences.
moves.first_failure: you will phrase it as a question and nobody will treat it as a view.
moves.observable: the minutes record your view against your name
moves.retire_when: people turn to you before the decision closes
moves.author: claude-draft

indirect_variant.behaviour: Send the decision-owner your one change and the reason the day before, in writing, under your name.
indirect_variant.observable: the decision-owner asks you to make the point in the room

moves.trigger: the first half of each weekly meeting
moves.behaviour: Bring one quiet colleague in by name, with a question you know they can answer.
moves.first_failure: you will ask it in the last five minutes, when nobody is listening.
moves.observable: a colleague who rarely speaks said something in the first half
moves.retire_when: the quiet end of the table speaks without being brought in
moves.author: claude-draft

moves.trigger: a standing hour, weekly, alone, in the calendar
moves.behaviour: Keep one hour of the old craft. Deliberately. Defend it like a meeting.
moves.first_failure: the hour will be the first thing you cancel.
moves.observable: the hour survived the week
moves.retire_when: the new work stops feeling like a substitute
moves.author: jim

indirect_variant.behaviour: Keep the craft hour on your own work, out of the team's sight, and defend it.
indirect_variant.observable: the hour survived the week and touched nothing the team now owns

moves.trigger: the standing craft hour, weekly
moves.behaviour: Finish one small piece of the old craft to your own standard, inside the hour.
moves.first_failure: you will start something too big and leave it half made. Size it to the hour.
moves.observable: a finished piece exists, and it came out of the hour
moves.retire_when: you can name what the craft still gives you that the new job does not
moves.author: claude-draft

moves.trigger: the craft hour, once a month, with a team member who now does the work
moves.behaviour: Teach one thing you know about the craft, then leave the work with them.
moves.first_failure: you will take the work back to show them. Keep your hands off it.
moves.observable: they did the work in the hour and you did not touch it
moves.retire_when: they bring you a question you cannot answer
moves.author: claude-draft

indirect_variant.behaviour: Ask a team member to show you how they now do the craft, and ask one question.
indirect_variant.observable: they showed the work, you asked one question, and the work stayed theirs

moves.trigger: any introduction where somebody else describes you
moves.behaviour: Give them the sentence first. One clause, the thing that makes you unusual, said as an asset.
moves.first_failure: your first version will be a CV. Cut it to one clause.
moves.observable: somebody uses your line back to you
moves.retire_when: the line arrives before you do
moves.author: jim

indirect_variant.behaviour: Send the introducer your one-clause sentence the day before, so it arrives in their voice.
indirect_variant.observable: the introducer uses your clause, or something close to it, when they introduce you

moves.trigger: the first meeting after an introduction that used your line
moves.behaviour: After the line, give one example of it at work, named and checkable, in under a minute.
moves.first_failure: you will pick the example that impresses you, and it will need explaining.
moves.observable: the other person asks a follow-up question about the example
moves.retire_when: people tell your example back to you
moves.author: claude-draft

indirect_variant.behaviour: Send the example afterwards in a short note, with the document or link that shows it.
indirect_variant.observable: the reply asks a question about the example

moves.trigger: a one-to-one with each person who regularly refers work to you, once a quarter
moves.behaviour: Tell them the kind of problem to send your way, in one sentence they can repeat.
moves.first_failure: you will describe everything you can do, and they will remember none of it.
moves.observable: a referral arrives that fits the sentence
moves.retire_when: work arrives that you did not go looking for
moves.author: claude-draft

moves.trigger: the first one-to-one with your own boss, fortnightly
moves.behaviour: Ask what the job is judged on in nine months. Write it down in front of them.
moves.first_failure: you will accept the first answer, which is the job description. Ask twice.
moves.observable: the answer exists on paper and your boss watched you write it
moves.retire_when: you can say the three criteria without looking
moves.author: jim

indirect_variant.behaviour: Bring a one-page draft of what the job is judged on. Ask your boss to correct it.
indirect_variant.observable: the draft comes back with your boss's edits on it, and you both keep the corrected copy

moves.trigger: the fortnightly one-to-one with your boss, from the second month
moves.behaviour: Report one piece of work against one written criterion. Ask whether it counted.
moves.first_failure: you will report activity, your boss will nod, and you will learn nothing. Name the criterion first.
moves.observable: your boss says which criterion the work moved, or that it moved none
moves.retire_when: your boss opens the one-to-one by asking about a criterion
moves.author: claude-draft

indirect_variant.behaviour: Send the criteria list before the one-to-one with this week's work marked against each. Ask for corrections.
indirect_variant.observable: the marked list comes back with your boss's corrections on it

moves.trigger: the first one-to-one with each new starter on your team
moves.behaviour: Write the three criteria their job is judged on, hand them the page, and ask what is missing.
moves.first_failure: you will write the job description again. Write what you will judge them on in nine months.
moves.observable: the new starter holds a page of criteria in your handwriting, with their additions on it
moves.retire_when: nobody on your team has to ask what they are judged on
moves.author: claude-draft

lines.message: To a colleague you trust: "I have agreed to this more than once and not moved. This week I am doing the small version."
lines.lean_into: Saying it out loud to one person is allowed to count as the first rep. It is the part that gets you moving.
lines.watch_for: turning the admission into a long account of why
lines.off_the_table: a promise of the full version
lines.format: a one-to-one with a peer, before the rep
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: To your own boss: "Hold me to one thing by Friday. I will tell you whether I met the threshold."
lines.lean_into: You are allowed to borrow somebody else's attention to get started. Most people move faster when someone is expecting them.
lines.watch_for: setting a threshold so low it is safe
lines.off_the_table: asking your boss to manage the rest of it
lines.format: the one-to-one with your boss
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: To your coach: "The thing I keep avoiding protects something. I want to know what before I push harder."
lines.lean_into: You are allowed to be curious about the avoidance before you fight it. What it protects is usually worth knowing.
lines.watch_for: using the curiosity as one more reason to wait
lines.off_the_table: a verdict on your character
lines.format: the coaching session
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "The firm's view is in the deck. Mine is narrower, and I'd like to put it to you."
lines.lean_into: the one point you would argue for if the firm had never taken it up
lines.watch_for: saying we through the whole meeting until your point dissolves into the firm's
lines.off_the_table: any client relationship or result the firm won without you
lines.format: to the client lead, in a meeting the firm's name got you into
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "If this point is useful to you, call me directly. Here's my number."
lines.lean_into: the follow-up question, which tells you the point landed
lines.watch_for: handing over the firm's general contact card out of habit
lines.off_the_table: any suggestion that the firm is lesser without you
lines.format: to the client contact who asked the follow-up, as the meeting breaks up
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "I'd like to put my name to the note that goes to the client after this meeting."
lines.lean_into: the partner's own interest in the client hearing a sharp view
lines.watch_for: asking in a way that invites a no
lines.off_the_table: authorship of any part of the work you did not write
lines.format: to the engagement partner, before the client meeting
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: To your team: "The decision is made. Here is what ends, and here is what I am keeping for you."
lines.lean_into: You are allowed to say the loss plainly. It is the steadiest ground you have in the first team meeting.
lines.watch_for: sliding into the upside in the same breath
lines.off_the_table: any claim that you chose the decision, or that it costs nothing
lines.format: the first team meeting after the announcement
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: To your own boss: "Tell me what I can share in full and by when, so my team hears it from me first."
lines.lean_into: You are allowed to ask for the facts before you carry them. The people above you want it carried well too.
lines.watch_for: agreeing to carry it before you know what is in it
lines.off_the_table: a promise to your team that your boss has not cleared
lines.format: the one-to-one with your boss before the team hears
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: To a report who asks you to reverse it: "I cannot change the decision. I can change how we carry it, and I want your say in that."
lines.lean_into: You are allowed to hold the line and still open the door. People take the first better when the second is real.
lines.watch_for: hinting that you would reverse it if you could
lines.off_the_table: reversing the decision, or blaming the people who made it
lines.format: one-to-ones in the first month
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "Here's what this gets you and here's what it costs you. Tell me if I've got the cost wrong."
lines.lean_into: their account of the cost, which is where the agreement gets made
lines.watch_for: arguing with their cost the moment they give it
lines.off_the_table: any promise to one blocker that the others would not hear
lines.format: to each blocker, alone, before the meeting
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "Can I bring the options on one page, so the room can decide on the day?"
lines.lean_into: the chair's own wish to end the stalemate
lines.watch_for: a page with one real option and the rest there for show
lines.off_the_table: a recommendation presented as the only choice
lines.format: to the chair, before the agenda goes out
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "I don't run any of your teams. I'm asking you to decide today, from this page."
lines.lean_into: the preparation you did one by one; the room already knows what is on the page
lines.watch_for: apologising for asking
lines.off_the_table: authority you do not hold
lines.format: to the room, in the meeting where the decision is stuck
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: To your own boss: "The work runs well. I want a problem I do not know how to solve yet."
lines.lean_into: You are allowed to say it runs well and still want more. Both are true, and your boss can use the second.
lines.watch_for: sounding as if you are complaining about the job
lines.off_the_table: a request for a promotion or a new title
lines.format: the one-to-one with your boss
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: To the owner of a meeting you want to sit in on: "Could I sit in next month as a learner? I want to understand the problem you are working on."
lines.lean_into: Curiosity about somebody's problem is a generous thing to bring. You are allowed to lead with it.
lines.watch_for: offering advice in the first meeting
lines.off_the_table: any claim on their territory or their decisions
lines.format: a short message, or a word after a meeting you both attend
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: To your team: "I am spending one meeting a month outside our work. You run things while I am there."
lines.lean_into: You are allowed to step out for an hour. Your team gets a turn at the front while you do.
lines.watch_for: checking in on them during the meeting
lines.off_the_table: stepping back from the work you are accountable for
lines.format: the team meeting
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "Can you give me the meeting that came from? I want to know what you saw."
lines.lean_into: the moment straight after the feedback, while you are still curious
lines.watch_for: asking in a tone that sounds like a challenge
lines.off_the_table: that the feedback is wrong
lines.format: said to the person giving the feedback, in the same conversation
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "I've got the steering meeting next week. Would you watch how I handle the pushback and tell me after?"
lines.lean_into: meetings where you already know there will be tension
lines.watch_for: choosing an easy meeting so the feedback comes back kind
lines.off_the_table: that you need them to tell you who you are
lines.format: a short request to your manager a few days before a named meeting
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "I've heard too soft and too hard from different people. I'm going to work from the situations and leave the adjectives."
lines.lean_into: your notes, where the situations are written down with dates
lines.watch_for: trying to work out who said which, and why
lines.off_the_table: that either description was unfair
lines.format: said to your mentor or sponsor in a one-to-one
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "I did the analysis in this section. I'd like to be the one who takes the client through it."
lines.lean_into: the prep call, while the deck is still being divided up and nobody has claimed the sections
lines.watch_for: asking in a way that sounds like an apology, so it is easy to say no to
lines.off_the_table: that the presenter did nothing, or that the whole deck is yours
lines.format: said to the account lead in the prep call before the client meeting
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "When you present this, would you name the team who built it? I've put the names on the first slide."
lines.lean_into: the hour after the draft is finished, when you are still proud of it
lines.watch_for: leaving your own name off the list to look generous
lines.off_the_table: that you are owed credit in the room personally
lines.format: a short message to the presenter the day before
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "Happy for you to present it. If the client asks how it was done, send the question to me."
lines.lean_into: the follow-up questions, where you know the work better than anyone in the room
lines.watch_for: answering the client's follow-up through the presenter because it feels easier
lines.off_the_table: taking the presentation from the person who owns the relationship
lines.format: said to the presenter when the meeting is agreed, and repeated in the confirming email
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "I picked you for this because you're the least experienced person who can do it, and that's the point."
lines.lean_into: the reason you picked them, said plainly
lines.watch_for: adding so many caveats that the piece sounds like a test
lines.off_the_table: a promise that you will fix it if it goes wrong
lines.format: to the junior, when you hand the piece over
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "[Name] drafted this section. I've reviewed it, and they'll lead the next one."
lines.lean_into: your review, which is what the client pays you for
lines.watch_for: presenting the section yourself so it goes smoothly
lines.off_the_table: that senior people did the drafting
lines.format: to the client lead, when the reviewed work goes over
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "It came back short. It's going back with one fix, and it stays with them."
lines.lean_into: the review itself; a named fix teaches more than a rewrite
lines.watch_for: agreeing to take it back this one time
lines.off_the_table: that the deadline does not matter
lines.format: to your co-lead, when they suggest you take the work back
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: To your leadership team: "When I move a meeting, read it as the calendar. When an act of mine means more, I will say so."
lines.lean_into: Telling people how to read you gives them permission to stop guessing, and you get the hours back.
lines.watch_for: explaining every act after the fact, which reads as spin
lines.off_the_table: a promise that none of your acts carry weight
lines.format: the next leadership team meeting
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: To a peer you trust: "What did people take from my last decision? Give me the reading and keep the names."
lines.lean_into: You are allowed to want to know how it landed. Asking one trusted person is enough to start.
lines.watch_for: arguing with the reading when you hear it
lines.off_the_table: who said what
lines.format: a coffee or a walk, away from your office
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: To your direct reports: "If you want to know what something I did means, ask me. I would sooner answer than have you guess."
lines.lean_into: Your door already reads as a signal. You are allowed to make that signal an open one.
lines.watch_for: answering with a paragraph when a sentence will do
lines.off_the_table: commentary on acts that are somebody else's to explain
lines.format: the team meeting once, then one-to-ones whenever it comes up
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "My view is we should [position]. Here's the one reason that matters most."
lines.lean_into: decisions where your field changes the answer
lines.watch_for: burying the position under three paragraphs of context
lines.off_the_table: certainty you do not have
lines.format: the first line of the paragraph you send to the decision-owner before the meeting
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "Before you decide on this, would ten minutes with me help? I can tell you what it changes for you."
lines.lean_into: the week before a decision, when the decision-owner is still collecting views
lines.watch_for: offering help in general, which nobody books
lines.off_the_table: that you should make the decision
lines.format: a message to the decision-owner a week before the meeting
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "I'm happy to be the one you call on this. Please call before the decision, while I can still change it."
lines.lean_into: being the first call on questions in your field
lines.watch_for: answering after the decision and calling it helpful
lines.off_the_table: a say on decisions outside your field
lines.format: said to the decision-owner at the end of a meeting where your view was used
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "What they built here worked, and I am keeping the part that made it work." Said to the team.
lines.lean_into: your respect for your predecessor, said once and meant
lines.watch_for: praising them so often the team hears doubt
lines.off_the_table: any claim that you will run things the way they did
lines.format: the first team meeting you chair
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "What did they do that you would miss most if it went?" Said to the longest-serving person on the team.
lines.lean_into: listening: you can let this be the question people have been waiting to be asked
lines.watch_for: defending a change while they are still answering
lines.off_the_table: a promise to keep everything they name
lines.format: a one-to-one with the longest-serving person on the team
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "I will do some of this differently, and I will tell you each change before it happens." Said to the team.
lines.lean_into: plain speech, which a place that loved its last leader will trust
lines.watch_for: calling a change a continuation
lines.off_the_table: comparisons with your predecessor, in either direction
lines.format: the team meeting, and the note that follows it
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "I cannot judge your work the way you can, so I need your standard to hold it to." Said to each function head.
lines.lean_into: the question: you learn fast when you let yourself ask
lines.watch_for: nodding at jargon you did not follow
lines.off_the_table: any pretence of expertise in their field
lines.format: the monthly with each function head
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "Walk me through a call you got wrong last year and what you look for now." Said to the function head.
lines.lean_into: curiosity about how experts think, which you can show openly
lines.watch_for: turning the story into an assessment of them
lines.off_the_table: using the story against them; if it will feed a judgement, say so first
lines.format: a one-to-one with the head, away from the review meeting
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "I will not sign this off until I understand what would make it fail." Said to the function head.
lines.lean_into: your accountability, which is the reason you get to ask
lines.watch_for: signing because the expert is impatient
lines.off_the_table: overruling the expert on the technical call
lines.format: the sign-off meeting, before the signature
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "I can't see most of what happens at your level. Tell me one thing I'm getting wrong."
lines.lean_into: the silence after the question; let it run
lines.watch_for: filling the silence with an example of your own
lines.off_the_table: any promise to act before you have heard the whole of it
lines.format: to one person at the monthly skip-level
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "I hold skip-levels with your team every month. I'll tell you what comes up about the work."
lines.lean_into: the manager's own interest in hearing what gets lost on the way up
lines.watch_for: turning the skip-level notes into a verdict on the manager
lines.off_the_table: confidentiality you cannot keep, and anything gathered on the manager behind their back
lines.format: to each manager whose team you meet, before the first skip-level
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "You told me what was slowing you down. Here's what I changed, and here's what I couldn't."
lines.lean_into: the part you could not change; saying it is what brings the next note
lines.watch_for: listing only the wins
lines.off_the_table: that the fix was your idea
lines.format: to the same group, at the next skip-level
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "Here is one number I think we have stopped looking at." Said to the operational meeting.
lines.lean_into: the data, where you are on firm ground
lines.watch_for: adding who caused it
lines.off_the_table: any judgement of your predecessor
lines.format: the weekly operational meeting
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "What would you need to see before this worried you?" Said to the person most sure things are fine.
lines.lean_into: curiosity: you can want to know where their line is before you argue about it
lines.watch_for: arguing with their answer in the same breath
lines.off_the_table: any claim that you have already found the fix
lines.format: a one-to-one with that person, before the next meeting
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "I will keep reporting this number every month until somebody owns it." Said to your boss.
lines.lean_into: persistence, which you have more of than anyone in the room
lines.watch_for: letting it drop after the first polite silence
lines.off_the_table: taking ownership of the problem yourself
lines.format: your one-to-one with your boss
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "Some things between us change this month, and I want you to hear them from me first." Said to each former peer.
lines.lean_into: the friendship: you have their trust already, and you can spend it on saying the hard part
lines.watch_for: joking about the new title so it sounds smaller
lines.off_the_table: any promise that nothing will change
lines.format: a one-to-one with each former peer, in a room with a door
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "When you disagree with a call I make, tell me first, and tell me directly." Said to each former peer.
lines.lean_into: your record for listening, which they already know
lines.watch_for: going quiet when they do disagree, which tells them the offer was for show
lines.off_the_table: a vote on the decisions that are now yours
lines.format: the same one-to-one, at the end
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "This one is my decision. Here is why I made it." Said to the former peer it affects most.
lines.lean_into: explaining your reasoning, which you do well
lines.watch_for: reopening the decision because the person is a friend
lines.off_the_table: an apology for having the job
lines.format: the team meeting where the decision is announced
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "In this role I intend to [what you will do]. Here's the first thing I'm starting on."
lines.lean_into: the first line of the announcement, before the role description
lines.watch_for: opening with your title and the company's language
lines.off_the_table: results you have not delivered yet
lines.format: the first line of your announcement email or post
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "Before I send this, would you read the first line and tell me if it sounds like me?"
lines.lean_into: people who have heard you talk about the work
lines.watch_for: asking five people and averaging their edits
lines.off_the_table: that the draft needs anyone's approval to be yours
lines.format: said to your sponsor, or a colleague who knows how you talk
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "Keep the house style for the layout. The first paragraph stays in my words."
lines.lean_into: the paragraph where you say what you intend
lines.watch_for: letting the edit sand the intention back into a job description
lines.off_the_table: rewriting the organisation's own messages
lines.format: said to whoever edits the announcement before it goes out
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "I'm here to win your work, and I'd like a second meeting on the problem you described."
lines.lean_into: the part of the conversation about their problem, where you know more than they expected
lines.watch_for: drifting back into describing how you would do the work as the ask gets close
lines.off_the_table: any promise about who will staff it before the scope exists
lines.format: to the buyer, at the end of the first meeting
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "Can we put a date in now for a working session with your team?"
lines.lean_into: the moment the buyer describes the problem a second time
lines.watch_for: softening the ask into an offer to send something over
lines.off_the_table: a discount offered before they have asked about price
lines.format: to the buyer, before either of you stands up
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "I'll send a proposal once we've agreed the scope together, so it prices the right thing."
lines.lean_into: what you know about how work goes wrong when the scope is guessed
lines.watch_for: sending the proposal that evening to look keen
lines.off_the_table: a price before the scope
lines.format: to a buyer who asks for a proposal after one call
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "From now on [successor] runs this day to day, and I'll stay on the review."
lines.lean_into: your confidence in the successor, said with them in the room
lines.watch_for: adding that the client can still call you any time
lines.off_the_table: that you will keep doing the work behind them
lines.format: to the client, in a meeting the successor attends
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "I want to hand this account on fully this quarter. Will you back me if the client pushes?"
lines.lean_into: the new job, which is the one your boss hired you to do
lines.watch_for: framing it as a favour to you
lines.off_the_table: a handover date you have not agreed with the successor
lines.format: to your own boss, before you tell the client
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "That one's with [successor] now. I've copied them in, and they'll come back to you."
lines.lean_into: the speed of the successor's reply, which is what the client wanted
lines.watch_for: answering the question first and copying them in afterwards
lines.off_the_table: that you have stopped caring about the client
lines.format: to the client who calls you about work you have handed on
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "I'm the quiet one in these meetings. When I speak, it's because I've thought it through."
lines.lean_into: the written prep before the meeting, where your thinking is clearest
lines.watch_for: apologising for being quiet before you have said anything
lines.off_the_table: that you will become the loudest voice in the room
lines.format: said to your manager in a one-to-one
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "Could you bring me in early on the first item? I've got one point on it."
lines.lean_into: items where you have done the reading others have not
lines.watch_for: asking to be brought in and then passing when the chair does it
lines.off_the_table: that the chair will make your point for you
lines.format: a message to the chair on the morning of the meeting
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "I'd like to take that away and come back to you with a view by the end of the week."
lines.lean_into: the time after the meeting, when you can think without an audience
lines.watch_for: promising a view and letting the deadline slide, which turns quiet into absent
lines.off_the_table: that you owe an answer on the spot to every question
lines.format: said out loud in the meeting, to whoever asked the question
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: To somebody close to you outside work: "I miss the work I was best at, and I am keeping an hour of it."
lines.lean_into: You are allowed to miss it. Saying so out loud takes some of the weight off.
lines.watch_for: turning the missing into a complaint about the new job
lines.off_the_table: any plan to go back to the old role
lines.format: outside work, over dinner or on a walk
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: To whoever holds your calendar: "That weekly hour is protected. Move anything else before you move it."
lines.lean_into: You are allowed to ask for help defending the hour. The person who holds the calendar can guard it better than you can.
lines.watch_for: moving it yourself the first time something urgent arrives
lines.off_the_table: an explanation of what the hour is for
lines.format: the calendar conversation, once
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: To the person who now does your old job: "It is yours. If I start doing it for you, tell me."
lines.lean_into: Handing it over cleanly frees you to keep the craft for yourself, and they will trust the hour you keep.
lines.watch_for: offering fixes on their work that you would have made
lines.off_the_table: reviewing their work for your own satisfaction
lines.format: a one-to-one in the first month of the handover
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "I'm the [discipline] person who also [second discipline]. That's why people bring me the problems that sit between the two."
lines.lean_into: the problems that sit across two teams, where nobody else has both halves
lines.watch_for: adding a third and fourth thing until the sentence is a CV again
lines.off_the_table: any title or credential you do not hold
lines.format: the first sentence you say when someone introduces you, in any meeting
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "When you introduce me tomorrow, could you use this line? It's the quickest way in."
lines.lean_into: introductions by people who already rate your work
lines.watch_for: sending a paragraph and letting them pick the part they like
lines.off_the_table: that they should oversell you
lines.format: a message to the person introducing you, the day before
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "I'd send that one to someone else. What I'm good for is [one clause]."
lines.lean_into: the moment someone files you under the wrong heading
lines.watch_for: saying yes to the wrong work because it is flattering to be asked
lines.off_the_table: that you can still do everything you have ever done
lines.format: said to a colleague who brings you work that fits someone else
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "I want to be judged on the right things, so I would like us to agree them now." Said to your boss.
lines.lean_into: the first fortnight, while asking still reads as keen
lines.watch_for: saying yes to every request so nobody can say you did not deliver
lines.off_the_table: any claim that you already know what the job asks
lines.format: the first one-to-one with your boss
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "Here is my draft of what this job is judged on. What would you change?" Said to your boss.
lines.lean_into: the page: you think best in writing, so you can bring the draft and let it do the asking
lines.watch_for: apologising for the draft before they have read it
lines.off_the_table: a request for more budget, people or title; this conversation is about criteria
lines.format: a one-page draft taken into the one-to-one
lines.author: claude-draft

lines.message: "Before I take that on, which of the three does it count towards?" Said to whoever hands you the work.
lines.lean_into: the moment a new request arrives, while the criteria are fresh in both your heads
lines.watch_for: taking the work first and asking later
lines.off_the_table: refusing the work; you are asking where it fits
lines.format: the corridor, the call or the email where new work gets handed over
lines.author: claude-draft
